# Spar 0.7.1

**Spar 0.7.1 sets real problems at your level, with a smaller bridge problem
first when the next one needs something you haven't shown yet. It also adds
review sessions, several accounts on one device, a rebuilt onboarding, and
stops LeetCode from disconnecting you every time you press Test.**

## The coach picks problems at your level

- **A ladder, not a leap.** Before setting the next problem, the coach names
  the mechanism it needs that you haven't shown on your own yet. If there is
  one, it sets a smaller bridge problem first. Before Sum Root to Leaf Numbers,
  for example, it might ask you to list every root-to-leaf path.
- **Real problems are checked against your rating.** A LeetCode or Codeforces
  problem priced outside the window that fits you comes back unassigned, with
  that window, unless the coach says why the stretch is deliberate. The coach
  searches by rating and reads two or three candidates before choosing.
- **Coaching settings, per Track.** Choose when Spar writes a problem instead
  of assigning a real one, and which lenses to go deeper on (mention, teach or
  drill). You can change both from a menu beside the challenge without going
  to Settings.
- **Old challenges can come back.** The coach can set a past challenge again
  with `reopen_challenge`.
- **Notebooks that diagnose.** Track notebooks record strengths, gaps named as
  the missing thinking, how you work, what helped and the plan, rather than a
  replay of each challenge. A new learner notebook records what is true of you
  across every Track. The notebook dialog has This Track and About you tabs.
  Your `user.md` is a real file you can open.

## Review sessions

- **Open a review session from History.** Pick cards yourself, take what is
  due, or take the ones slipping most. The coach sets each review as a real
  problem and judges your attempt against the card.

## Accounts

- **Several accounts on one device.** Each account has its own store,
  workspaces and skills. Switching keeps both signed in, and signing out
  removes only that account. The sign-in screen can go back to another
  account without a password.
- **LeetCode and Codeforces sign in through your own browser.** Sign-in opens
  an installed Chrome, Edge, Brave or Chromium on a profile Spar owns, so
  password managers, passkeys and Google sign-in work.

## Onboarding

- **A rebuilt first run.** Arrival, a warm-up, your notebook and your first
  Track are one sequence, and the window opens out only when it's done.

## The window

- **Errors show in the bottom-right toast**, the same place as everything
  else Spar tells you, and wrap so the whole sentence is readable. An error
  that says to reconnect has a Settings button.
- **New thread rows** for reopened challenges, file reviews and challenge-mix
  changes. Code peeks are highlighted in the file's language, and typing in
  the editor no longer redraws the thread.

## Fixes

- **LeetCode no longer disconnects on Test.** Cloudflare, in front of
  LeetCode, challenges some code (a comment with a run of colons was enough).
  Spar used to read that as an expired session, stop sending your cookie, and
  then get challenged on every request after it. A challenge now never
  disconnects you. The run is retried from a hidden page on leetcode.com,
  which passes the check, with no window and no extra browser. A session that
  really was refused reconnects on its own when your Spar browser profile is
  still signed in.
- Sync no longer stalls when one session hasn't reached the server yet. That
  session's rows wait while everything else syncs.

## Downloads

| Your machine | File |
| --- | --- |
| Mac, Apple silicon | `Spar-0.7.1-arm64.dmg` |
| Mac, Intel | `Spar-0.7.1.dmg` |
| Windows | `Spar-0.7.1-x64.exe` |
| Linux | `Spar-0.7.1-x86_64.AppImage` or `Spar-0.7.1-amd64.deb` |

## Known limits

- This open distribution is unsigned. macOS Gatekeeper or Windows SmartScreen
  may ask you to approve the first launch, and those platforms may require a
  manual installer step for an update.
- Linux AppImage installations can self-update when the runtime supports it;
  `.deb` installations stay managed by the system package manager.
